fields.meta_title: Sales Funnel Landing Page: 4 Examples and Steps | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A sales funnel landing page is the first step on the path to a sale. Follow four funnels past checkout and build yours from one prompt.
fields.h1: Build a Sales Funnel Landing Page and Every Step After It
fields.hero_description: Build a sales funnel landing page plus the checkout and upsell pages behind it, with one record per buyer in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: The Funnel Behind the Landing Page
fields.features_subheading: Visitors see one page at a time. Emergent builds what runs behind each, down to the email sent when someone leaves checkout.
fields.feature_1:
Each step on its own URL

Describe the pages in the order a buyer sees them: landing page, offer, checkout, upsell, confirmation. Emergent builds each one at its own URL and links them in that sequence.
fields.feature_2:
Card payments through Stripe

Connect your Stripe account and the checkout takes cards, with an add-on as a checkbox beside the total. Every charge is written to the buyer's row with its product and amount.
fields.feature_3:
One buyer record across every page

Follow each person from the landing page to the thank-you page under one visitor ID. Their email, the source that sent them, each purchase, and any refund sit on one row you own.
fields.feature_4:
Conversion counts for each step

Ask for a dashboard and Emergent builds one that counts visitors at every page and divides each count by the one before. The step with the lowest rate is listed first.
fields.feature_5:
Emails for people who stop halfway

Send a reminder to anyone who reaches checkout and leaves without paying, and a different email to those who opted in but never bought. Each send is logged on the buyer's row.
fields.feature_6:
The whole funnel in your repository

Export the funnel's pages and buyer table to your GitHub on paid plans. Host it on Emergent at a custom domain, which uses credits, or run the code on your own server.

fields.usecase_heading: Where Each Funnel Makes or Loses the Sale
fields.tab_content_1:
A $12 add-on ticked at checkout

Wildroot Skincare sends its ad clicks to a page for a $34 vitamin C serum. At checkout, a checkbox adds a $12 travel cleanser to the order. Once the card clears, the next page offers a 3-month refill for $79, accepted with a click and no card form. The order row records which offers the buyer took.
fields.tab_content_2:
The calendar opens at $20,000 a month

Owners who apply for Oxbow Coaching's $4,000 program answer four questions after a short training video. Anyone reporting $20,000 or more in monthly revenue goes straight to Odile Varga's booking calendar. Everyone else is offered the $149 self-paced course instead.
fields.tab_content_3:
Three answers decide which of four boxes

On a phone, Copperkiln Coffee Roasters asks three questions: how you brew, how dark you like it, and how many cups you drink a week. The answers pick one of four subscription boxes, and the next screen offers that box with the first bag at half price. Each answer set is saved next to the order it led to.
fields.tab_content_4:
720 opt-ins and the step that lost most of them

Every Monday at 8 AM, Sumwise Academy gets a report on its freelancer funnel: a free invoice checklist, then a $9 template kit, then a $197 bookkeeping course. Last week 720 people took the checklist, 86 bought the kit, and 14 went on to the course. The kit page lost the most people and gets rewritten first.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Sales Funnel Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Plan a sales funnel landing page and each page after it in seven steps, then build it and see where buyers drop off.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Start from the offer at the end
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Give every page a single job
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Match the first page to the traffic
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Price the add-on well below the order
fields.howto_step_1_des: Work backward from the product the funnel exists to sell. A $30 product can follow a free opt-in directly. A program priced in the thousands asks for more trust; put a video or an application in front of its price.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the pages down in sequence, then give each one a job: collect an email, make the case, take payment, offer an add-on, confirm the order. A page asked to do two of those jobs at once tends to do neither well.
fields.howto_step_3_des: The landing page should repeat the promise of the ad or email that sent the visit. Someone who clicked an ad for a serum expects to see that serum, not the store's home page. Build a separate first page for each promise you advertise.
fields.howto_step_4_des: An order bump works when it is small next to the order and fits with it, such as a travel size or a printed guide. Place it as a checkbox above the pay button. Track how often it is ticked and whether completed checkouts drop after adding it.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Show the bigger offer on the page that follows a successful charge, when the buyer has already decided. With the card saved at checkout, accepting takes one click. Make declining as plain with a No thanks link, and send both answers to the confirmation page.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Plan an email for each exit
fields.howto_step_6_des: Someone who opted in and never bought needs a different message from someone who left at checkout. Decide what each group gets and when it is sent. Stop the sequence the moment a person buys, because a discount email after a full-price order costs trust.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Compare how many people reach each page with the page before it. The lowest rate shows where to work next. Change one page at a time and compare whole weeks before and after, since daily numbers move with traffic.

This page defines the term for the answer box, settles landing page versus funnel in one FAQ answer, then follows four funnels to the step that decides the money: an add-on at checkout, an application that gates a sales call, a quiz that picks the offer, and a weekly report that names the weakest step.

claims_to_source: An order bump is a small add-on offered on the checkout page, usually as a checkbox, before the buyer pays
A one-click upsell is offered after payment and charges the card already on file without asking for it again
A landing page is a standalone page built for one campaign goal, separate from a site's main navigation
A sales funnel is the sequence of steps a prospect moves through on the way to a purchase
A tripwire is a low-priced first offer made to turn a new lead into a paying customer
Stripe can save a customer's payment method during checkout so it can be charged again later
